What could I do in Srbac in order to prevent the escalation of problems of the kind that happened in other municipalities? I really can't help you with that, really. I stand by the fact and I am repeating that when the municipalities had to deal with their own problems, I had my problems. I went to meetings in Banja Luka in order to find out where I could find oil, fuel, wood. I didn't want to pursue municipal policies. I may have heard some information, but that wasn't my position, that was not my job. I couldn't cry. It was not up to me to sit and cry. I had to act, I had to work. You have to understand that I was saying this in order to give you a real picture. Everybody did things in their own way. Our situation was good. We had communication with the Croats all the time. We never discussed that. I even brought some Croatian newspapers, Arena, who spoke positively about the co-operation between our two municipalities, and that it was really incredible to see things like that happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milincic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender those pages, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be added too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Milincic, you've painted yourself repeatedly --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I kindly ask Mr. Tieger to provide a reference as to where it was that I said that we could not control their birth rate? That I said that we could not control their birth rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was quoting from the transcript at 18448, and as a general matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we continue. It's a quote from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It can be discussed --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's an allegation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It can be discussed --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Mr. Tieger's allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you can raise it when this is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Milincic, you have depicted yourself repeatedly as a humanist, concerned wholly with legality, as I understood your testimony. In fact, if we turn to P921, page 80 of the English and page 55 of the B/C/S, you came out very early for the taking of international personnel as hostages in order to improve the RS situation, didn't you? At page -- this is the transcript of the 24th Session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska held on the 8th of January, 1993, and I'll quote what you said: "We also have something to blackmail them with. Homeini, in his time, held a very small number of Muslims in the American embassy in Tehran and he sure did shake America quite well. Well, we also have enough of those white men or others and that can be used as our weapon." That's what you advocated to the Assembly at the beginning of January 1993, didn't you, Mr. Milincic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: I have to help you a bit with that. This was taken out of context. You haven't read out all of it. I told the story about the lamb and the wolf there, the fable. We're always blamed. Let us do something so that they understand that they need to talk to us. And I said: Let's take some people, let's keep them here. Maybe they will come to pick them up and then talk to us. And then you played something two years after my statement of mine -- now, you see when I made this statement, two years in advance, two years before the pilots. Don't tell me that I was the architect of that idea for the pilots to be taken. Really. This can be used very wrongly. I said something, but as our people say, they're not taking account of this. Let's take their people, let's bring them in. They will come to get them and then we'll talk to them: Hey, people, we don't want war. And now two years after that statement of mine in Banja Luka, you are showing those pilots there two years later exactly. And I chuckled and said: Are you saying that I was the architect of that idea for arrests, hostages, whatever? I mean, I was telling this story, this fable about the lamb and the wolf. It's the lamb's fault for drinking water downstream and you've taken it out of context totally. We are not being taken seriously. We want to talk, so if they won't do it in any other way, let's bring them in by force and then they will come to pick them up. And now you are playing this which two years later. Give me the time when I said this in Banja Luka and give me the time when this thing with the pilots happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't mention the word "pilots," Mr. Milincic, but thank you for raising that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, because ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, did you ask for your remarks in the Assembly to be translated into some kind of document, that this be considered that way?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: AR Krajina, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was just shown to you, our Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this just free discussion or did you ask for this to be adopted? Was there a vote on some proposal of yours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: No, no, I took part in this discussion. I mean, some people even laughed sort of -- well, leave all of that aside, fairy tales, fables, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: Well, this was just my discussion out of despair. If you mean the wolf and the lamb, oh, yes, yes. I wanted to say in literary terms that they are not respecting us and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about things that happened in other municipalities. Can you tell us how many incidents there were in your municipality and who were they aimed against? Was it only against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: I mentioned the Malesevics a moment ago, then the Vejinovics, Kladari, I don't even remember the name of the family. People were beaten up, looted -- it's really hard to speak about all these small incidents. But percentage-wise there were more Serbs, of course, yes, 21.000. Now these people of ours who returned, say came on holiday -- Serbs who came on holiday, they were mistreated. They were robbed, if I can use that word, intimidated, blackmailed, by these so-called heros.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But foreigners don't know on the basis of last names what the ethnic background would be of Malesevic, Vejinovic, et cetera. What was their ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: Serbs. Malesevic in Gornja Lepenica, Vejinovic in Razboj [phoen] and then a Serb family in Kladari. So they were the victims of these gangs that would come at night, robbing them, asking for money, fuel, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the attitude of the authorities against these crimes committed against Serbs, Muslims, Croats? Did the authorities instigate that, conceal it, or stop it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: I personally at the Crisis Staff beseeched, begged, insisted, I said: These hoodlums who are mistreating innocent people, whoever it may be, stop them from doing that, don't let them do that, take weapons from them, bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for what you heard, those rumours, what was happening in other municipalities in the Krajina, regardless of whether they were true or not, exaggerated or not, did you have information to the effect that this was a product of the conduct of the authorities, our authorities in these municipalities? What was the attitude of our authorities towards that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: The authorities dealt with these individuals who were renegades, if I can put it that way, one, two, three. So there were shoot-outs, there was shooting. The authorities did not agree with that. They did not want to justify that. They opposed it. They took away their weapons, disarmed them, as I said. Say they would beat people up, say they'd beat up a Serb and steal his tractor or a Golf car and then say they'd walk on the Golf car, a Serb would do that to another Serb, destroy his car. That's the kind of situation that would happen then at the time. I mean, to this day we have such situations in municipalities that people would have this kind of thing happening to them, even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Repeat the number, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D09746. Could we have the last paragraph displayed now, 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You saw there where the Prosecutor stopped. Can you tell us what else is contained in this paragraph and that is not stated there, over there they stopped with a representative of the Serb people?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: We did not want a war, that's why we had a plebiscite. We thought that the Cutileiro Plan was our salvation. We were happy that all of that would be brought to an end; however, we know what happened. We know what Izetbegovic did --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Professor. Just tell us this. Paragraph 22, was all of it displayed or is there another subparagraph in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: I cannot find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph above the witness acknowledgement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We can no longer hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whenever we'd speak on the phone, you would always suggest to me: Take this all into account, try to pacify the extremists, protect people's property. Quite simply, perhaps you have the best conditions, better than other municipalities. Take refugees in, provide supplies to people. Those were the things that we mentioned all the time, and through that I saw you as a person who saw that Srbac could be successful in this. Oppose these adventurers and -- I don't know if I got the point here. We had the best conditions and also this contact with the Croats on the other side. Srbac as a municipality was a municipality. It was even suspected a bit by other neighbouring municipalities because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to tell us the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second, Mr. Karadzic. I'm asking for planning purposes. How much longer do you need for your re-direct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will rise for two minutes. --- Break taken at 2.46 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, for the remainder of the session, we'll sit -- we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, without Judge Lattanzi, who is -- who should attend another meeting. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Professor Milincic, whether the facts in this statement are correct, truthful?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: Everything that was said, from the establishment, the questions, the problems I mentioned here, all of that is contained in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you say "contained," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MILINCIC
utterances.text: I mean that they are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This statement, does it reflect truthfully your position with regard to these developments --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's not appropriate to try to 92 ter this statement. That's exactly what's going on. We're going through a reverse attestation process and that's not appropriate here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is exactly what we were left to do after the interventions during the cross-examination, is to show that the circumstances under which the statement was taken was such that the information is reliable is not something that was fed to him by the Defence. And then we will tender the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then he can ask about the one paragraph he was asking about, that's certainly appropriate. But to try to bootstrap impeachment that they consider effective, they need -- to respond to into a basis for introducing the whole statement that has been determined to be largely irrelevant by the Court is clearly inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson and Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber is minded to admit paragraph 22 in its entirety of this statement, but if the Defence is going to tender the entire statement in order to show the nature or process how witness statements are being made, Mr. Karadzic should go one paragraph -- each paragraph one by one, how the -- what was the effect and how the paragraph was formulated. At this stage we'll admit paragraph 22 of this document in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit Number D4187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we show paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I'm -- I don't think it's a good way to show the paragraph first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already asked about departures earlier on. I've already asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't follow you, Mr. Karadzic. You were going to re-examine the witness about the departure which was referred to during the cross-examination of Mr. Tieger or you are going to deal with the manner and the process how witness statement was prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, both, Excellencies. First of all, to establish whether it is the way the Prosecution claims, whether words were put there. Actually, it's better for me to ask, not to talk about this in front of the witness. Let me ask the witness and then you will decide what you will admit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I didn't cross-examine on the issue of how many Muslims left or didn't leave Srbac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I understood departure as departure from the policy, whether SDS departed from the policy in which Mr. Karadzic expressed in the rally or something like that. I misunderstood. I didn't see -- I didn't read this para 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't see why Dr. Karadzic can't display to the witness the paragraph and ask him whether or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's a leading question --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, it's not a leading question. The question would be: Is this your words or did someone put these words into your mouth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, no, you didn't understand my question. I asked the purpose of that question was which, but he said: Yes, both, in order to elicit the statement -- evidence contained in the statement. To show the statement itself is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think the object here is to admit certain paragraphs of the statement. So to do that simply to try to show whether or not these are his words or whether somebody put words in his mouth, that's the object of what we're trying to do. I don't think it's leading to ask: Is this your words or did someone put this in -- this is not what you said? If he says it's his words, it shows that the statement itself and the information that was brought to this Court by this witness is his own formulation and not something that was suggested by the Defence. And that's completely proper in response to what Mr. Tieger has done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, having heard the witness's statement that they are his words, I don't think that exercise would help the Chamber at all, whether it --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But then the Chamber -- what the Chamber has done is exclude our statement, including paragraphs which you acknowledge were relevant to Dr. Karadzic's case, required us to lead the witness live, and then given the Prosecution 100 per cent benefit of what it wanted from the statement while depriving us of the right to have what we want from the statement admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's not a game. I mean, it's the Defence that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, you can sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, the Status Conference will take place at 15.30. We should withdraw from this courtroom at 1500 hours sharp. There's a problem. We'll allow the question but not today. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Mr. Milincic, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
